implementation: Use SI internally; set one convention for impact angle (angle between incoming velocity and target normal, 0° = normal impact). Store source angle text separately. Distinguish plate thickness along local normal from projected effective path.
exit_test: Automated tests for angle conversion, plate-normal calculation, mass/energy conservation accounting and units; no ballistic claims yet.
must_not_do: Do not silently convert 30° from a historical table to the game convention without verifying datum.

implementation: Make a flat coupon with documented density/elastic properties, then run tensile/compressive/shear/impact-style tests appropriate to the chosen particle model. Fit bond stiffness, strength, plasticity, fracture energy, and damping from macro response.
exit_test: Elastic wave speed and coupon response stable under particle refinement; energy error bounded; no penetration test tuning before coupons behave.
must_not_do: Do not treat each circle as an actual metallurgical grain. Particle size is a numerical discretization length until the model is explicitly calibrated.

implementation: Start with a simple rigid ogive and controlled 20 mm experimental case (S21); then oblique/ricochet case (S20). Use 2D only with declared plane-strain/axisymmetric limitations; 3D is needed for fully spatial cap/body, yaw and fragment effects.
exit_test: Penetration depth/crater/bulge trends match published experimental ranges and solver converges as particle spacing is reduced. Record uncertainty.
must_not_do: Do not tune directly to Tiger data before generic solver convergence.

implementation: Add body and AP cap as distinct materials, ballistic wind cap as a different component, and failure/erosion. Verify projectile post-impact state and plate damage, not just whether a hole exists.
exit_test: Correct qualitative modes across velocity, thickness and obliquity: crater/plug/penetration/ricochet/projectile deformation; energy budget closes.
must_not_do: Do not simulate Pzgr39 as a single rigid disk or only use its total mass and muzzle speed.

stage: 4 - Tiger plate samples and variant geometry
implementation: Build exact panel geometry (Tiger I frontal panels first, then Tiger II 150 mm glacis and 180 mm production turret front); assign source-specific sample records and uncertainty ranges to material properties. Early Porsche-pattern turret is a separate geometry/material variant.
exit_test: CAD geometry reviewed against an archival drawing; source angle basis resolved. Every property has provenance and confidence/unknown marker.
must_not_do: Do not use a single “Tiger armour” scalar or assign early turret metallurgy to all Tiger II production armour.

implementation: Use range-indexed historical curves only after target hardness, angle definition, round variant and penetration criterion are reconciled. Also validate dent, cracking/spall, seams, and repeated-hit damage from the actual test reports.
exit_test: Report curve fit across multiple ranges/angles and show residual error; run repeated sampled shots; compare outcomes against tests without a lookup-table decision in the impact solver.
must_not_do: Do not equate a historical table penetration figure to deterministic “always passes” logic.

implementation: Represent known variability in plate properties, welds, defects, thickness, impact point, velocity and angle. Run repeat shots with logged seed. Estimate P(perforation | material, projectile, geometry, speed, angle) from outcomes; retain confidence intervals.
exit_test: Repeated-run outcome curve has expected trend and uncertainty, and fits only source-supported ballistic test datasets.
must_not_do: Do not inject an arbitrary random chance after a deterministic hit calculation just to imitate probability.

implementation: Implement APCR as multi-material core/jacket, then APDS/APFSDS separately; HEAT needs a shaped-charge jet model; HESH needs stress-wave/scab model; HE needs blast/fragmentation.
exit_test: Each ammunition family passes its own validation cases and declared applicability range.
must_not_do: Do not share one generic penetration routine across AP, APCR, APFSDS, HEAT and HESH.
